title: Becoming a Better Procrastinator
coreMove: Manage time by choosing the neglect: protect one consequential commitment first, cap active work, and let merely respectable tasks stay undone.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who treat all delay as failure
exampleSpecs.stakes: distinguish accidental postponement from values-led neglect
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show Gregg Krech's reversal through a named person choosing which neglect is deliberate

exampleSpecs.audience: people who believe better ordering will fit every worthy priority
exampleSpecs.stakes: see the flaw in a comforting productivity parable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Stephen Covey's jar to show that worthy priorities can still exceed capacity

exampleSpecs.stakes: protect valued work before reactive demands consume the day
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show Jessica Abel's pay-yourself-first rule as a time allocation

exampleSpecs.audience: people who keep options open to protect satisfaction
exampleSpecs.stakes: see why reversibility can keep comparison alive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Daniel Gilbert's poster study to show finality deepening appreciation

exampleSpecs.audience: workers hiding avoidance inside many active projects
exampleSpecs.stakes: limit active work so hard meaningful tasks cannot be dodged
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show too many open projects becoming an escape from the difficult one

exampleSpecs.audience: people keeping every attractive life path open
exampleSpecs.stakes: commit without treating unchosen paths as proof of failure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show settling as the condition for making one path real
